disclaimer: Educational decision support only. Similar symptoms can have non-disease causes. Confirm diagnosis with a KVK, agricultural extension officer, or plant pathologist. Use only products registered for the crop and disease locally and follow the current label.

symptoms: Tan elongated lesions enlarge and merge
Severe infection dries leaves and reduces grain filling
prevention: Manage residue and use balanced fertilizer
treatment: Use a registered foliar fungicide only when risk justifies it
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Lesions merge and destroy large leaf areas
prevention: Use resistant hybrids and crop rotation
treatment: Use a registered fungicide only for high-risk susceptible crops
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Water-soaked lesions with alternating light and dark bands
Sheaths, leaves, and ears may rot with small sclerotia
prevention: Use tolerant hybrids and recommended spacing
Remove lower infected leaves where advised and manage residue
treatment: Improve airflow and avoid excess nitrogen
Seek local advice on biological or registered fungicide options
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Pale yellow stripes run along leaves
White downy growth appears beneath leaves; plants become stunted and barren
prevention: Use resistant hybrids and treated seed
Remove volunteer maize and rogue infected plants early
treatment: Remove plants and follow locally approved seed-treatment guidance
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Lower stalk tissues become soft or shredded
Plants lodge and internal pith may be pink or salmon coloured
prevention: Use resistant hybrids and balanced fertility
Reduce drought and insect stress and harvest promptly
treatment: Harvest lodged or affected fields early if safe
Dry grain rapidly and test suspect grain for mycotoxins
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails

symptoms: Lower stalks contain many tiny black specks and shredded pith
prevention: Reduce drought stress and maintain soil fertility
treatment: Harvest promptly and improve water and residue management next season
escalate_when: Symptoms spread rapidly or affect stems, roots, panicles, ears, bunches, bolls, or fruit
Diagnosis is uncertain, several plants are affected, or initial management fails
